posts.body:
Traders just repriced next week's Fed meeting hard: the odds of a rate hike jumped to **70%** on the CME FedWatch gauge after hot wholesale inflation data and crude oil ripping past **$100/barrel**. On top of that, a *second* hike by December is now sitting near 60% as the Iran conflict keeps inflation pressure entrenched. The last data card before the meeting — Friday's CPI — could swing this either way. ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/10/the-likelihood-of-a-fed-interest-rate-hike-next-week-just-got-a-lot-higher.html))

This is exactly the kind of binary event prediction markets were built for. A 70% implied probability isn't certainty — it's a tradeable line. If you think the Fed blinks on growth or that CPI comes in soft, the *no-hike* side is paying you 30 cents on the dollar to be contrarian. If you think oil at $100 forces their hand, you fade the doubters.

On EventTrader you can take a direct position on the meeting outcome, the December follow-through, or the CPI print itself — with tight two-sided books and on-chain settlement. When macro moves this fast, the edge goes to whoever prices the tail before the crowd does. **Where's your line on 70%?**
posts.title: Fed Hike Odds Spike to 70% — Is the Market Pricing This Right?

[16:29] <sedited> if we can't guarantee what's in those release notes, then we should not ship the feature imo.
[16:29] <darosior> Making a difference between passive and active attackers here make sense, but i'm concerned it would be hard to translate into an actionable information for users, and end up being a footgun.
[16:29] <sipa> Right, but "honest but curious" is trivially false, if every behavior is "honest". That's a term that's used in cryptographic protocol with a well-defined prescription of how honest parties operate. Bitcoin doesn't have any of those.
[16:29] <instagibbs> fanquake ok that note is wrong, two txs can be linked at the blockchain layer even with perfect impl
[16:30] <bitcoin-git> [🟣 bitcoin] fanquake opened pull request #36222: [30.x] More Backports (30.x...even_more_30_x_backports) 🔵 https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36222
[16:30] <instagibbs> "not be linkable at the networking layer" maybe
[16:30] <andrewtoth> instagibbs "otherwise unrelated" though

[16:26] <darosior> Are shooting for "If you are not a reachable node, operating only on Tor, then we guarantee the transactions you broadcast won't be easily correlated with each other"?
[16:26] <instagibbs> If our privacy model is "honest but curious", then AFAIK we cover that. It's also about user expectations
[16:27] <instagibbs> but that;s hard to to communicate, and weaker
[16:27] <instagibbs> "what's honest but curious": they follow protocol, but write everything down, say
[16:27] <fanquake> The claims in https://bitcoincore.org/en/releases/31.0/ are "Their IP address (and thus geolocation) is never known to the recipients." & "If the originator sends two otherwise unrelated transactions, they will not be linkable. This is because a separate connection is used for broadcasting each transaction. "
[16:27] <darosior> instagibbs: so, passive observer?
[16:27] <instagibbs> vs active probing, protcool violations
[16:27] <sedited> yeah, that seems very clear.
[16:28] <instagibbs> darosior they follow the stated protocol
[16:28] <instagibbs> whatever that means
[16:28] <instagibbs> the prior issue we had and fixed violated this
[16:28] <sipa> There isn't even a well-defined "honest" behavior for nodes.
[16:28] <instagibbs> sipa handwaving here
